# HIP 20894: A Variable Catalogued as tet02 Tau

*The available measurements sketch a star through its position, motion, classification and recorded light—but leave important questions unanswered.*

A star’s catalog entry can look like a compact biography. For HIP 20894, the SIMBAD database supplies a name used in astronomy, a variable-star classification, a spectral type and measurements of position and motion. These details give a precise outline of the object, while also showing how much a single record does not tell us.

SIMBAD lists HIP 20894 as “tet02 Tau” and classifies it as a delta Scuti variable. That classification is a useful starting point, not a complete account of the star’s changing light: the entry provided here does not give a period, an amplitude or a record of how its brightness varies over time. It identifies the kind of variable assigned to the object, but not the particulars of its changes. ([SIMBAD, HIP 20894](https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/sim-id?Ident=HIP%2020894))

The database also lists a spectral type of A7III, with a C quality flag. This is a separate description from the variability classification: one records a spectral type, the other a variable-star category. SIMBAD’s quality scale runs from A, its best quality, to E, its worst, so the C flag is part of the record’s assessment rather than an additional stellar property. The entry does not supply further explanation of the classification or its basis.

Position and motion offer another view. SIMBAD gives the star’s ICRS coordinates for epoch J2000 as right ascension 04h 28m 39.7416s and declination +15° 52′ 15.149″. The same entry reports proper motion of 106.148 milliarcseconds per year in right ascension, with the declination component at −20.294 milliarcseconds per year. These figures describe its recorded location and motion across the sky; by themselves, they do not tell a reader what the star’s movement looks like to the unaided eye. The coordinates and proper motions are attributed to the 2020 Gaia catalogue entry in SIMBAD (2020yCat.1350....0G).

The record also lists a parallax of 21.8125 milliarcseconds, with an uncertainty of 0.3735 milliarcseconds, from that same catalogue. A radial velocity of 38.90 kilometres per second, with an uncertainty of 0.2, is credited to a 2004 paper (2004A&A...424..727P). These measurements describe different aspects of the star’s position and motion. Their presence in one record makes comparison possible, but does not by itself provide a narrative of the star’s history.
